tools.name: list_roots
tools.description:
Returns the filesystem roots the MCP client advertised for this session (cached from roots/list).

When to use: Call when another tool needs to resolve a relative path and you have no absolute context yet. Rarely needed — most DCC tools operate on in-memory scene data, not the client's workspace.

How to use:
- Takes no arguments; returns an empty array if the client sent no roots.
- Do not call repeatedly; roots change only on client reconnect.

tools.name: list_skills
tools.description:
Lists skills with load status (loaded, unloaded, error, skipped).

When to use: Browse availability or audit active skills. For ranked lookup, use search_skills.

How to use:
- status='loaded' for active skills, 'unloaded' for load candidates, 'skipped' for diagnostics.
- One bounded page (25 by default, 50 max). While 'truncated' is true, follow 'next_step' or pass offset=next_offset; 'total' is the full size.
- Then get_skill_info(skill_name=...) or load_skill(skill_name=...).

status.description: Load-status filter; 'all' returns skills, 'skipped' returns rejected package diagnostics.

include_skipped.description: Include skipped skill diagnostics with stable reason codes and suggested fixes.

limit.description: Maximum skills to return (default 25, hard cap 50).

offset.description: Skip this many skills after sorting by name; use the previous page's next_offset.

fields.description: Strict allow-list of per-skill fields. Omit for compact mode (name, stage, summary, tool_count, …).

tools.name: get_skill_info
tools.description:
Returns detailed metadata for one skill: description, tags, DCC binding, and full input schemas for every tool it declares.

When to use: Use when you already know the skill name and need to inspect its tools' schemas before committing to load_skill. Pair this with search_skills when deciding between candidates.

How to use:
- Inspecting alone does not make the tools callable; follow up with load_skill(skill_name=...) to activate them.
- Returns an error if the skill is unknown.

skill_name.description: Exact skill name as reported by list_skills / search_skills.

tools.name: load_skill
tools.description:
Loads discovered skills, registers their tools, and emits tools/list_changed.

When to use: After search_skills/list_skills/get_skill_info identifies the skill. Idempotent for already-loaded skills.

How to use:
- Pass skill_name or skill_names.
- Groups activate by default; set activate_groups=false for lazy group activation.
- Pass tool_group with one skill to activate only that group plus default-active groups.
- After success, call tools/list or the specific tool directly.

skill_name.description: Single skill to load; mutually exclusive with skill_names.

skill_names.description: Batch of skill names to load in one call.

activate_groups.description: Cascade-activate all declared tool groups after loading. Set false for lazy activation.

tool_group.description: Activate one group for a skill; defaults activate_groups=false and includes default-active groups.

tools.name: unload_skill
tools.description:
Unloads a previously loaded skill, unregisters its tools, and emits a tools/list_changed notification.

When to use: Use to free tool slots and shrink the tools/list token footprint once a workflow no longer needs a skill. Safe to call on an unloaded skill (no-op).

How to use:
- Pending tools/call requests against this skill will fail after unload — drain them first.
- To re-enable the skill later, call load_skill(skill_name=...).

skill_name.description: Exact skill name previously passed to load_skill.

tools.name: search_skills
tools.description:
Unified skill discovery. Ranks skills against query across name, description, search-hint, tags, and tool names; filters by tags/dcc/scope. Matching skipped skill directories are returned in `skipped` with diagnostics.

When to use: Start here when you need a capability but don't know the skill name. Call with no args to browse by trust scope (Admin>System>User>Repo).

How to use:
- Keep query short (2-4 keywords); combine with tags/dcc/scope.
- After a hit, call load_skill(skill_name=...).

query.description: Short keyword phrase (2-4 words). Leave empty to browse by scope.

tags.description: Filter by tags (all must match; case-insensitive).

scope.description: Filter by trust scope (Admin > System > User > Repo).

limit.description: Cap the number of results (default 20, max 100).

tools.name: activate_tool_group
tools.description:
Activates a tool group inside a loaded skill, making its members callable and emitting a tools/list_changed notification.

When to use: Call when tools/list surfaces a __group__<name> stub and you need the underlying tools. Progressive exposure keeps the default surface small until you opt in.

How to use:
- The parent skill must be loaded first; check list_skills(status='loaded') if unsure.
- After activation, re-run tools/list to see the newly available tools, then call them by name.

group_name.description: Group name as shown in the __group__<name> stub.

skill_name.description: Optional owning skill from a scoped group stub. Omit for legacy catalog-wide activation.

tools.name: deactivate_tool_group
tools.description:
Deactivates a tool group, collapsing its members back into a __group__<name> stub and emitting a tools/list_changed notification.

When to use: Use to shrink the active tool surface once a sub-workflow is done, to stay within the client's token budget. Group tools remain on disk — only their visibility changes.

How to use:
- Idempotent; calling on an already-inactive group is a safe no-op.
- To bring the tools back, call activate_tool_group(group_name=...).

group_name.description: Group name previously passed to activate_tool_group.

skill_name.description: Optional owning skill from a scoped group stub. Omit for legacy catalog-wide deactivation.

tools.name: search_tools
tools.description:
Full-text search over loaded tools and unloaded skill metadata. Unloaded hits come back as `skill_candidate` with `requires_load_skill: true` and a ready `load_hint` (#677).

When to use: Find a capability by keyword. If a hit is a skill_candidate, call `load_skill` with its `skill_name` first.

How to use:
- Short query; matches name, description, tags, schema keys.
- `include_stubs=true` shows `__skill__*` / `__group__*` for debug.
- `limit` caps each hit array (default 25, max 100).

query.description: Keyword matched against tool name, description, category, tags, and input-schema property names.

include_disabled.description: Also search tools inside inactive tool groups.

include_unloaded_skills.description: Include matching unloaded skills as `skill_candidate` results with a load_hint.

limit.description: Maximum entries returned for each of `tools` and `skill_candidates`.

tools.name: jobs_get_status
tools.description: Poll the status of an async tool-call job tracked by JobManager. Returns a JSON envelope with job_id, core_job_id, job_id_owner, parent_job_id, tool, status (pending|running|completed|failed|cancelled|interrupted), timestamps, progress, error, and optionally the final ToolResult once the job is terminal. A terminal result that starts adapter-owned work also exposes adapter_job_id and, when declared, its typed poll contract. Complements the `$/dcc.jobUpdated` SSE channel (#326) for polling-based clients. Returns isError=true with a human-readable message when the job id is unknown (never a JSON-RPC transport error).

job_id.description: UUID of the job to query

include_logs.description: Include captured stdout/stderr if any. Currently a no-op — JobManager does not capture logs; the flag is accepted for forward compatibility.

include_result.description: Include the job's final ToolResult when the job is in a terminal state (completed/failed). Ignored for pending/running jobs since no result exists yet.

tools.name: jobs_poll_contract
tools.description: Report how an async job type is polled to a terminal state. With `job_type`, returns the registered poll contract or `registered: false` plus a reason — a job type that is not registered cannot be waited on with --wait. Without `job_type`, lists every job type the unified poller tracks. Registration happens when a tool result declares a `poll` descriptor {owner, tool, arguments} or when the adapter registers the contract directly.

job_type.description: Tool name that starts the job (e.g. `houdini_render__render_rop`). Omit to list every registered job type.

tools.name: jobs_cleanup
tools.description: Purge terminal (completed/failed/cancelled/interrupted) jobs older than `older_than_hours` hours from JobManager and any attached storage backend. Non-terminal (pending/running) jobs are never removed regardless of age. Returns {removed: <count>} as structured content. Idempotent — repeated calls with the same window return 0 once the pruning horizon is reached.

older_than_hours.description: Prune terminal jobs whose last update is older than this many hours. Default: 24.

tools.name: register_tool
tools.description:
Dynamically register a new session-scoped tool from a ToolSpec.

When to use: When you need a one-off helper that executes DCC code on demand and you want it to appear in tools/list only for this session.

How to use:
- Provide tool_spec with at minimum name, description, and code.
- The returned tool_name is the callable identifier — use it in tools/call.
- Tool expires when the session ends or after ttl_secs (default 3600 s).

name.description: Tool base name: [a-zA-Z0-9_-], max 52 chars so the assigned dyn__ name stays within 64 chars.

code.description: Python code body. Use params dict for inputs.

parameters.description: JSON Schema properties map for tool inputs.

read_only_hint.description: Hint: tool does not mutate DCC state.

ttl_secs.description: How long the tool lives (seconds). Default 3600.

tools.name: deregister_tool
tools.description:
Remove a dynamically registered tool from this session.

When to use: After the agent no longer needs a tool registered via register_tool.

How to use:
- Pass the tool_name returned by register_tool.
- Returns success even if the tool has already expired.

tool_name.description: Assigned tool name returned by register_tool (starts with dyn__).

tools.name: list_dynamic_tools
tools.description:
List all non-expired dynamic tools registered by this session.

When to use: To audit which session-scoped tools are currently available, or to find their exact names before calling or deregistering them.

How to use: No parameters required.

tools.name: capture_current_view
tools.description: Atomically capture the configured view without changing presentation. Fail without publication if native capture resets camera or other measured state.

tools.name: contour
tools.description: Create bounded isosurfaces from a named single-component point scalar.

tools.name: dcc_introspect__eval
tools.description: Evaluate a bounded expression built from literals and allowlisted pure builtins, then return its repr. When to use: for small type, shape, ordering, or arithmetic checks. Use list_module, search, and signature for DCC APIs; attributes, imports, comprehensions, and dynamic builtins are unavailable.

expression.description: Short read-only Python expression to evaluate in the DCC interpreter.

tools.name: get_adapter_info
tools.description: Read pure adapter capabilities without touching the native host.

tools.name: qt_ui_inspector__list_windows
tools.description: List every top-level Qt window with object name, class, visibility, geometry, and child count.

tools.name: jobs_resume_context
tools.description: Check whether a checkpoint exists for a job and return resume context. When to use: before re-submitting an Interrupted job — retrieve saved state to pass as initial parameters so execution resumes from the last checkpoint. How to use: pass job_id; if checkpoint exists, pass context to the tool's next invocation.

job_id.description: ID of the interrupted job to resume.

tools.name: reopen_state
tools.description: Replace this isolated pipeline with an unchanged state saved by this running session.

data_directory.description: Optional workspace-confined directory of byte-identical copied single-file data. Copied PVSM must match a state saved by this current session; arbitrary external states remain rejected.

tools.description: Return the latest checkpoint state for a job. When to use: to inspect progress of a running or interrupted job. How to use: pass job_id; returns {saved_at, progress_hint, context} or {checkpoint: null} if no checkpoint exists.

job_id.description: Job ID to query checkpoint status for.

tools.name: dcc_diagnostics__audit_log

tools.name: inspect_presentation
tools.description: Read only existing views, representations, source-name bindings, cameras, materials, scalar palettes and legends; never creates display state.

tools.description: Validate candidate inputs against a structured recipe pack input schema. When to use: before recipes__apply or before dispatching recipe steps.

tools.name: edit_sphere

tools.name: create_sphere

tools.description: Regex-search exported names in a DCC module or attribute namespace. When to use: when you need to find a function but only remember part of its name. How to use: pass a regex pattern + module; use dcc_introspect__signature on hits.

pattern.description: Case-insensitive regex to match against exported names.

module.description: Module or attribute namespace to search, e.g. 'unreal.GeometryScript_BoneWeights'.

tools.name: dcc_feedback__report
tools.description: Report a bounded Finding v1 when installation, startup, dispatch, or a skill is blocked, degraded, has a workaround, or suggests an improvement. Supply phase, severity, intent, observed, expected, and exactly one repro.argv or repro.steps list; identify the subject with tool_slug or evidence.error_kind. Core auto-fills runtime versions, DCC identity, OS, fingerprint, and conservative redaction status before forwarding to the gateway. The original tool_name / blocker input remains accepted as a compatibility form.

tools.name: qt_ui_inspector__snapshot_tree
tools.description: Walk the Qt widget tree under a root and return it as a JSON-safe tree with depth and node-count budgets.

tools.name: inspect_pipeline
tools.description: Inspect sources, native geometry counts, host identity, and rendering prerequisites.

tools.name: dcc_introspect__list_module
tools.description: List exported names in a Python module or attribute namespace in the DCC interpreter. When to use: before writing a script — discover what functions are available without browsing offline docs. How to use: pass the dotted module path; use dcc_introspect__search to narrow results.

module.description: Dotted module or attribute namespace, e.g. 'maya.cmds' or 'bpy.ops.object'.

tools.name: dcc_introspect__signature
tools.description: Return the signature and docstring for a callable in the live DCC interpreter. When to use: when you have a function name from dcc_introspect__list_module or dcc_introspect__search and need parameter names and defaults. How to use: pass the fully-qualified name, e.g. 'maya.cmds.polyCube'.
